first.rationale: The two declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, and fixing a structural funnel leak compounds across all future cohorts, whereas promotional pricing (memory_73) mostly buys price-sensitive accounts whose lifetime value is exactly the segment the competitor can re-poach — poor fit for 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue'. So the intended action rests on memory_31 and memory_86, which makes them both the most consequential and the least verified for this objective: both were consolidated on proxy outcomes (first-week activation, completion rate, time-to-value), not on downstream qualified revenue or retention. That is precisely the gap that matters here. Cutting required signup fields in particular can lift activation while degrading lead qualification, routing volume and sales attention toward accounts that never become qualified revenue — and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted paths, so a thinner signup form could actively strip the routing signal that sends enterprise traffic to demo-request. I want the archived records to tell me whether either experiment tracked revenue-side or lead-quality outcomes at all, and over what horizon the 'durable' lift in memory_31 was measured. I am not verifying memory_73 or memory_57 because they underpin actions I am not taking this week; memory_91 is directionally aligned with activation_messaging, my fallback if onboarding evidence collapses. Running as a small guarded test with qualified-lead rate, enterprise-path routing, and paid conversion as pre-declared guardrails rather than a broad rollout, because the inherited evidence supports the proxy and not yet the objective.

final.rationale: Both records came back confirmed, and importantly they separate into two distinct levers with different risk profiles. exp_86 (shortened onboarding flow: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) touches the post-signup path only, so it cannot degrade lead qualification or divert enterprise traffic away from the demo-request path (memory_44). exp_31 (cutting signup fields: signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, retention -1%) is the lever that carries the lead-quality risk I flagged, and the archive partly confirms it: retention moved slightly negative and the qualified-revenue lift (+4%) is much smaller than the top-of-funnel lift (+15%), which is the signature of admitting weaker-fit accounts. So I am weighting the experiment toward the onboarding-flow shortening and treating signup-field reduction as the secondary, tightly-scoped component. Scope: SMB self-serve only, since exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB and neither record speaks to enterprise; the demo-request route stays untouched. Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 never measured qualified revenue at all, only completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, so its link to the primary objective is inferred rather than demonstrated — that is the main thing this run should establish. Pre-declared guardrails: qualified-lead rate, enterprise-path routing share, paid conversion, and 30-day retention, with a stop if retention drops beyond the -1% already seen. I am declining promotional_pricing (memory_73) despite the competitor's entry pricing because it defends the least durable revenue against a rival who can re-cut price, and both measured declines are funnel-structural, not price-structural. activation_messaging (memory_91) remains the fallback if the onboarding lift fails to reach revenue.
